reason: This passage from Judges 4 portrays regular people favorably overall. The Israelite people, despite initially described as doing evil, are ultimately presented as worthy of divine salvation and victorious against their oppressor. More notably, Jael—an ordinary woman with no official position or authority—is portrayed as remarkably heroic, courageous, and wise, becoming the instrument of Sisera's defeat and earning an honored place in the narrative. Even Deborah, while serving as a judge and prophetess (giving her some exceptional status), is depicted very favorably as a confident, wise leader. The regular Israelite soldiers are shown as willing to follow and ultimately victorious. In contrast, the unfavorable portrayals are reserved for foreign rulers (Jabin) and military commanders (Sisera). The text's trajectory shows regular people being divinely favored and empowered to overcome their oppressors.
